name: Tiger Woods
hints: Turned pro in 1996 after an outstanding amateur career, including three straight U.S. Amateur titles.
Born in Cypress, California, and played college golf at Stanford.
Has won 15 major championships across a two-decade span.
Long associated with Nike and known for an unmistakable fist-pump celebration.
Held all four major titles at once during 2000-2001, a feat nicknamed after him.
Completed one of sports' greatest comebacks by winning the 2019 Masters after years of injury, famous for wearing a red shirt every Sunday.

name: Jack Nicklaus
hints: Turned pro in 1961 after a standout amateur career at Ohio State.
Born in Columbus, Ohio.
Won major championships across four different decades, from the 1960s into the 1980s.
Also became one of the most prolific golf course designers in history.
Nicknamed 'The Golden Bear' for his blond hair and powerful build.
Holds the record for most men's major championships won, 18, capped by an unforgettable win at age 46 in the 1986 Masters.

name: Arnold Palmer
hints: Turned pro in 1954 and helped popularize golf on television.
Born in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, the son of a golf course superintendent.
Won 7 major championships during the late 1950s and 1960s.
One of the 'Big Three' golfers of the 1960s alongside Nicklaus and Player.
His army of passionate fans became famously known as 'Arnie's Army.'
Nicknamed 'The King,' he also lent his name to a half-lemonade, half-iced-tea drink still sold today.

name: Gary Player
hints: Turned pro in 1953 and became known for his relentless fitness regimen.
Born in Johannesburg, South Africa.
Won 9 major championships spread across three different decades.
Almost always wore all black on the course, even decades before it was common.
Nicknamed 'The Black Knight' or 'Mr. Fitness.'
One of only six golfers ever to complete the career Grand Slam, alongside Nicklaus, Hogan, Sarazen, Woods, and McIlroy.

name: Tom Watson
hints: Turned pro in 1971 after graduating from Stanford.
Born in Kansas City, Missouri.
Won 8 major championships, more than half of them Open Championships.
Famous for chipping in on the 17th hole to win the 1982 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach.
Nearly won an improbable 6th Open Championship in 2009 at age 59.
Engaged in a legendary head-to-head battle with Jack Nicklaus at the 1977 Open, forever remembered as the 'Duel in the Sun.'

name: Seve Ballesteros
hints: Turned pro in 1974 as a teenager from a farming family.
Born in Pedrena, Spain.
Won 5 major championships, including the Masters twice.
A driving force behind Europe's Ryder Cup resurgence, both as player and later as captain.
Famed for his flair and creative recovery shots from seemingly impossible positions.
Won the 1979 Open Championship partly from a parking lot, forever earning him the nickname 'the car park champion.'

name: Nick Faldo
hints: Turned pro in 1976 and later rebuilt his swing from scratch mid-career.
Born in Welwyn Garden City, England.
Won 6 major championships, three of them at the Masters.
Went on to become a leading, blunt golf broadcaster after his playing career.
Captained Europe's Ryder Cup team in 2008.
Famously outlasted Greg Norman's historic final-round collapse to win the 1996 Masters.

name: Greg Norman
hints: Turned pro in 1976 and spent 331 total weeks ranked world No. 1.
Born in Mount Isa, Queensland, Australia.
Won 2 major championships, both Open Championships.
Known for his aggressive play and bleach-blond hair.
Nicknamed 'The Shark,' with a logo to match.
Later became the driving force and CEO behind the LIV Golf league, and suffered one of the most infamous final-round collapses in Masters history.

name: Phil Mickelson
hints: Turned pro in 1992 and won a PGA Tour event while still an amateur.
Born in San Diego, California.
Won 6 major championships, including 3 Masters titles.
Left the PGA Tour to become a founding star of the LIV Golf league in 2022.
Nicknamed 'Lefty,' known for his go-for-broke style despite naturally being right-handed.
Became the oldest major champion in history at the 2021 PGA Championship, winning at age 50.

name: Ernie Els
hints: Turned pro in 1989 and is known for one of the smoothest swings in golf.
Born in Johannesburg, South Africa.
Won 4 major championships, split evenly between two different majors.
Also built a successful wine and golf course design business.
Nicknamed 'The Big Easy' for his relaxed tempo and demeanor.
Won the 2012 Open Championship largely because Adam Scott bogeyed the final four holes.

name: Vijay Singh
hints: Turned pro in 1982 and became famous for hitting more range balls than anyone on tour.
Born in Lautoka, Fiji.
Won 3 major championships, two of them PGA Championships.
The first male golfer from Asia ever to reach world No. 1.
Named PGA Tour Player of the Year in 2004 at age 41.
Won 9 PGA Tour events in a single standout season, 2004, known simply as 'Vijay' to golf fans worldwide.

name: Padraig Harrington
hints: Turned pro in 1995 after a career as an accountant.
Born in Dublin, Ireland.
Won 3 major championships in a two-year span, 2007-2008.
Later captained Europe's Ryder Cup team in 2021.
Won back-to-back Open Championships, the first European to do so in decades.
Has become a dominant force on the PGA Tour Champions in his 50s, known for his relentless work ethic on the range throughout his career.

name: Justin Leonard
hints: Turned pro in 1994 after an outstanding amateur career at the University of Texas.
Born in Dallas, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 1997 Open Championship at Royal Troon.
Known for one of the greatest comeback wins in Ryder Cup history, the 'Miracle at Brookline.'
Sank a legendary long birdie putt on the 17th hole at Brookline in the 1999 Ryder Cup.
That putt sparked such a wild celebration that fans and players overran the green before Jose Maria Olazabal could even attempt his own putt.

name: Davis Love III
hints: Turned pro in 1985, the son of a PGA teaching professional.
Born in Charlotte, North Carolina.
Won 1 major championship, the 1997 PGA Championship.
Won 21 PGA Tour titles over a two-decade career.
Captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in both 2012 and 2016.
One of the most respected veterans and Ryder Cup figures of his generation, known for his smooth, powerful swing.

name: Fred Couples
hints: Turned pro in 1980 and became known for one of the most effortless swings in golf.
Born in Seattle, Washington.
Won 1 major championship, the 1992 Masters.
Was world No. 1 and PGA Player of the Year in 1991-92.
Remains a fan favorite and dominant force on the PGA Tour Champions.
Nicknamed 'Boom Boom' for his prodigious driving distance off the tee.

name: Payne Stewart
hints: Turned pro in 1979 and was instantly recognizable for his old-fashioned style.
Born in Springfield, Missouri.
Won 3 major championships, including 2 U.S. Opens.
Famous for wearing plus-fours (knickers) and colorful tam o'shanter caps on course.
Won the 1999 U.S. Open at Pinehurst with a dramatic final-hole putt.
Died tragically in a plane crash just months after that final major win.

name: Ben Hogan
hints: Turned pro in the 1930s and rose from a difficult childhood to golf greatness.
Born in Dublin, Texas.
Won 9 major championships across a career interrupted by both World War II and personal tragedy.
Author of the influential instructional book 'Five Lessons: The Modern Fundamentals of Golf.'
Regarded as one of the greatest ball-strikers the game has ever seen.
Nearly killed in a 1949 car accident, then miraculously returned to win 3 majors in a single year, 1953, later dubbed the 'Triple Crown.'

name: Sam Snead
hints: Turned pro in 1934 and played competitively into his 60s.
Born in Ashwood, Virginia.
Won 7 major championships across three different decades.
Famous for his trademark straw hat, worn throughout his career.
Holds the record for most PGA Tour wins ever, 82.
Nicknamed 'Slammin' Sammy' for his power off the tee, yet famously never won the U.S. Open despite four runner-up finishes.

name: Byron Nelson
hints: Turned pro in 1932 and later became a respected golf broadcaster.
Born in Fort Worth, Texas.
Won 5 major championships in a relatively short competitive career.
A PGA Tour event, the AT&T Byron Nelson, is named in his honor.
Won 18 total PGA Tour events in a single season, a record that still stands.
Won an astonishing 11 consecutive PGA Tour events in 1945, widely considered the single most untouchable record in golf.

name: Bobby Jones
hints: Never turned professional, remaining an amateur his entire competitive career.
Born in Atlanta, Georgia, and trained originally as a lawyer.
Won 7 major championships (by modern count) purely as an amateur golfer.
Co-founded Augusta National Golf Club and the Masters Tournament after retiring.
Retired from top competition at just 28 years old.
Completed the original Grand Slam in 1930, winning all four majors of that era in a single year, then walked away from competitive golf for good.

name: Walter Hagen
hints: Turned pro in 1912 and helped elevate professional golfers' social standing.
Born in Rochester, New York.
Won 11 major championships, more than all but three golfers in history.
Often credited with popularizing golf as a viable, glamorous profession.
Nicknamed 'The Haig,' famous for his flamboyant lifestyle and showmanship.
Won 4 consecutive PGA Championships from 1924 through 1927, a title-defense streak never matched since.

name: Rory McIlroy
hints: Turned pro in 2007 as a teenager out of Holywood, Northern Ireland.
Known for his combination of power off the tee and a smooth, unforced tempo.
Won his first major, the 2011 U.S. Open, by a record-setting margin.
Widely regarded as the leading European golfer of his generation.
Spent over a decade chasing the career Grand Slam after winning three of the four majors by his mid-20s.
Finally completed the career Grand Slam by winning the 2025 Masters in a playoff.

name: Jon Rahm
hints: Turned pro in 2016 after a standout college career at Arizona State.
Born in Barrika, Spain.
Won the 2021 U.S. Open and the 2023 Masters.
Often mentioned alongside Seve Ballesteros as Spain's greatest golfing talent.
Left the PGA Tour for a lucrative move to LIV Golf in late 2023.
Was born with a clubfoot, giving him an unusually short, powerful swing that's instantly recognizable on tour.

name: Scottie Scheffler
hints: Turned pro in 2018 after an All-American career at the University of Texas.
Born in Ridgewood, New Jersey, but raised in Dallas, Texas.
Has won multiple Masters titles, including in 2022 and 2024.
Widely regarded as the most dominant golfer in the world in the mid-2020s.
Known for an unorthodox, rock-solid putting grip that stands out immediately on tour.
Known for spending long, uninterrupted stretches as the world's top-ranked golfer, all while maintaining a notably quiet, methodical demeanor.

name: Jordan Spieth
hints: Turned pro in 2012 after starring at the University of Texas.
Born in Dallas, Texas.
Won 3 of the 4 majors before turning 24, missing only the PGA Championship.
Known for his exceptional putting and precise course management.
Won the 2015 Masters and 2015 U.S. Open in the same season.
Suffered a painful, historic final-round collapse at the 2016 Masters after leading by 5 shots, and has spent years since chasing the career Grand Slam.

name: Justin Thomas
hints: Turned pro in 2013, the son of a PGA club professional.
Born in Louisville, Kentucky.
Has won 2 PGA Championships, in 2017 and 2022.
A key member of recent U.S. Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup teams.
Known simply by his initials, 'JT,' among fans and fellow players.
Shot a record-tying 59 in a PGA Tour round early in his career, and is close childhood friends with Jordan Spieth.

name: Dustin Johnson
hints: Turned pro in 2007 and became known for elite athleticism and effortless power.
Born in Columbia, South Carolina.
Won the 2016 U.S. Open and the 2020 Masters.
Left the PGA Tour to become a founding LIV Golf star in 2022.
Spent over 130 weeks ranked world No. 1 across his career.
Won the pandemic-delayed 2020 Masters by a record 5 strokes, played in November instead of its usual spring date.

name: Brooks Koepka
hints: Turned pro in 2012 and built his early career playing on European and Challenge Tours.
Born in West Palm Beach, Florida.
Has won 5 major championships, split between two different majors.
Known for elite fitness and a notably calm demeanor under pressure.
Won the 2023 PGA Championship as one of LIV Golf's biggest stars.
Known specifically for saving his best golf for major championship weeks, capped by winning back-to-back U.S. Opens in 2017-2018 and back-to-back PGA Championships in 2018-2019.

name: Collin Morikawa
hints: Turned pro in 2019 after an outstanding college career at Cal Berkeley.
Born in Los Angeles, California.
Won two different major championships before turning 25.
Considered one of the most accurate ball-strikers of his generation.
Won the 2020 PGA Championship in just his second career major start.
Also won the 2021 Open Championship at Royal St George's, making him one of the fastest players ever to complete wins at two different majors.

name: Xander Schauffele
hints: Turned pro in 2015 after playing college golf at San Diego State.
Born in San Diego, California, to a French father and Japanese-American mother.
Spent years as one of the best players in the world without a major title.
Known for a relaxed, understated personality despite his elite results.
Won Olympic gold in golf at the 2021 Tokyo Games.
Finally broke through by winning both the PGA Championship and the Open Championship in the same season, 2024.

name: Bryson DeChambeau
hints: Turned pro in 2016 after winning the NCAA title and U.S. Amateur in the same year.
Born in Modesto, California.
Won 2 U.S. Open championships, in 2020 and 2024.
Left the PGA Tour to join LIV Golf in 2022.
Nicknamed 'The Scientist' for his intensely analytical approach to the game.
Famously bulked up dramatically to add driving distance, then won the 2024 U.S. Open at Pinehurst with a dramatic closing bunker shot.

name: Viktor Hovland
hints: Turned pro in 2019 after winning the U.S. Amateur while at Oklahoma State.
Born in Oslo, Norway.
Has not yet won a major championship despite years among the world's elite.
Was low amateur at the 2019 Masters before turning professional.
A fan favorite for his outgoing, chatty personality on course.
Known for elite ball-striking long paired with a famously inconsistent short game, one of Norway's first true golf stars.

name: Matt Fitzpatrick
hints: Turned pro in 2014 after winning the U.S. Amateur while at Northwestern.
Born in Sheffield, England.
Won 1 major championship, the 2022 U.S. Open.
Known for one of the most compact, repeatable swings on tour.
Won the U.S. Amateur at Brookline in 2013.
Became the first golfer ever to win both the U.S. Amateur and U.S. Open at the very same course, nine years apart.

name: Shane Lowry
hints: Turned pro in 2009 after winning the Irish Open as an amateur.
Born in Clara, County Offaly, Ireland.
Won 1 major championship, the 2019 Open Championship.
Known for his warm, easygoing personality off the course.
A key contributor to recent European Ryder Cup teams.
Won that Open at Royal Portrush, Northern Ireland's first Open in decades, in front of an emotional, deafening home crowd.

name: Francesco Molinari
hints: Turned pro in 2002 and played alongside his brother Edoardo for years.
Born in Turin, Italy.
Won 1 major championship, the 2018 Open Championship.
Famous for his metronomic, error-free ball-striking during his 2018 peak.
Went undefeated in five matches at the 2018 Ryder Cup.
Won that Open at Carnoustie, becoming the first Italian golfer ever to win a men's major championship.

name: Adam Scott
hints: Turned pro in 2000 after being mentored early on by Greg Norman.
Born in Adelaide, Australia.
Won 1 major championship, the 2013 Masters.
Was among the first prominent players to popularize the long, anchored putter.
Reached world No. 1 in 2014.
Won that Masters in a playoff with a dramatic birdie putt, becoming the first Australian ever to win the tournament.

name: Sergio Garcia
hints: Turned pro in 1999 as a teenage prodigy from Spain.
Born in Borriol, Spain.
Won 1 major championship, the 2017 Masters.
Later joined LIV Golf as a team captain and owner.
Spent nearly two decades as one of the best players in the world without a major title.
Nicknamed 'El Nino,' he finally broke through by winning the 2017 Masters in a playoff, on what would have been Seve Ballesteros's 60th birthday.

name: Henrik Stenson
hints: Turned pro in 1999 and became known for one of the purest iron games in golf.
Born in Gothenburg, Sweden.
Won 1 major championship, the 2016 Open Championship.
Later served as the inaugural European captain courted by LIV Golf.
Became the first Swedish golfer ever to win a men's major championship.
Won that Open in a legendary duel with Phil Mickelson, in which both players shattered the previous major championship scoring record.

name: Zach Johnson
hints: Turned pro in 1998 after college golf at Drake University.
Born in Iowa City, Iowa.
Won 2 major championships, roughly eight years apart.
Known for his devout faith, often referencing it in victory speeches.
Later served as U.S. Ryder Cup captain in 2023.
Won the 2007 Masters by laying up on every par-5 all week, then won the 2015 Open Championship at St Andrews in a playoff.

name: Keegan Bradley
hints: Turned pro in 2008 after college golf at St. John's University.
Born in Woodstock, Vermont, nephew of LPGA Hall of Famer Pat Bradley.
Won 1 major championship, the 2011 PGA Championship, in his first career major start.
Was one of the last prominent players to use a long, anchored putter before it was banned.
Named U.S. Ryder Cup captain for the 2025 matches.
Pushed to make himself a playing captain for that Ryder Cup, an idea much discussed in golf media.

name: Gene Sarazen
hints: Turned pro in 1920 and rose from a childhood of manual labor to golf stardom.
Born in Harrison, New York, to Italian immigrant parents.
Won 7 major championships across the 1920s and 1930s.
Credited with inventing the modern sand wedge.
Nicknamed 'The Squire' for his dapper on-course style.
One of only six golfers ever to complete the career Grand Slam, famous for holing a 4-wood for double eagle at the 1935 Masters, the 'shot heard round the world.'

name: Lee Trevino
hints: Turned pro in 1960 after growing up caddying near Dallas, Texas.
Born in Dallas, Texas, to a family of modest means.
Won 6 major championships, evenly split across three different majors.
Survived being struck by lightning at the 1975 Western Open.
Known for his quick wit and constant chatter with fans and playing partners.
Nicknamed 'The Merry Mex' or 'Super Mex,' famously never won the Masters and often joked he disliked Augusta's course.

name: Raymond Floyd
hints: Turned pro in 1961 and had one of the longest winning careers in golf history.
Born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina.
Won 4 major championships spanning nearly two decades, from 1969 to 1986.
A fierce competitor known for his intense on-course stare.
Won the 1976 Masters by 8 shots, tying the tournament's 72-hole scoring record at the time.
Became the oldest U.S. Open champion in history when he won in 1986 at age 43.

name: Hale Irwin
hints: Turned pro in 1968 after also playing college football as a defensive back.
Born in Joplin, Missouri.
Won 3 U.S. Open championships across three different decades.
One of the most dominant players in PGA Tour Champions history after turning 50.
Became the oldest U.S. Open champion ever at the time, winning in 1990 at age 45.
Famous for a joyous, high-fiving sprint down the 18th fairway after his clinching putt in that 1990 win.

name: Curtis Strange
hints: Turned pro in 1976 after a standout college career at Wake Forest.
Born in Norfolk, Virginia.
Won 2 U.S. Open championships, back-to-back.
Later became a respected golf broadcaster.
Captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in 2002.
Won consecutive U.S. Opens in 1988 and 1989, the first golfer to do that since Ben Hogan in the early 1950s.

name: Mark O'Meara
hints: Turned pro in 1980 and became one of Isleworth's most recognizable club members.
Born in Goldsboro, North Carolina.
Won 2 major championships in the very same year.
Widely credited as an early mentor to a young Tiger Woods.
Won that year's Open Championship at Royal Birkdale in a four-hole playoff.
Won both the Masters and the Open Championship in 1998, at age 41, making him one of the oldest first-time major champions ever.

name: Ian Woosnam
hints: Turned pro in 1976 despite being one of the shortest players on tour.
Born in Oswestry, Wales.
Won 1 major championship, the 1991 Masters.
Reached world No. 1 the same year he won that Masters.
Later captained Europe's victorious 2006 Ryder Cup team.
Nicknamed 'Woosie,' known for hitting the ball a surprisingly long way from a notably compact frame.

name: Sandy Lyle
hints: Turned pro in 1977 after a standout amateur career in Scotland and England.
Born in Shrewsbury, England, to a Scottish golf professional father.
Won 2 major championships, three years apart.
A key figure in Europe's Ryder Cup resurgence of the 1980s.
Famously hit a 7-iron from a fairway bunker to set up his winning birdie at Augusta.
Became the first British golfer ever to win the Masters, having already won the 1985 Open Championship.

name: Bernhard Langer
hints: Turned pro in 1972 and battled the putting yips multiple times across his career.
Born in Anhausen, West Germany.
Won 2 Masters titles, eight years apart.
Continued winning senior majors well into his 60s.
Widely regarded as the greatest player in PGA Tour Champions history.
Became the first German golfer ever to win a major championship, winning the Masters in both 1985 and 1993.

name: Jose Maria Olazabal
hints: Turned pro in 1985 and formed a legendary Ryder Cup partnership with Seve Ballesteros.
Born in Hondarribia, Spain.
Won 2 Masters titles, five years apart.
Considered one of the greatest short-game players of his generation.
Overcame a severe case of rheumatoid arthritis in his feet mid-career to keep competing.
Later captained Europe's deeply emotional 2012 Ryder Cup win, dedicated to the memory of Seve Ballesteros.

name: Corey Pavin
hints: Turned pro in 1982 after a decorated amateur career at UCLA.
Born in Oxnard, California.
Won 1 major championship, the 1995 U.S. Open.
Known throughout his career for a scrappy, creative short game despite modest length.
Captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in 2010.
Famously hit a 4-wood to four feet on the final hole at Shinnecock Hills to seal that U.S. Open win.

name: Retief Goosen
hints: Turned pro in 1990 and survived being struck by lightning as a teenager.
Born in Pietersburg, South Africa.
Won 2 U.S. Open championships, three years apart.
One of the calmest putters under pressure of his generation.
Nicknamed 'The Goose' for his unflappable, ice-cool demeanor.
Won his first U.S. Open, in 2001, after an 18-hole playoff, then won again in 2004.

name: Angel Cabrera
hints: Turned pro in 1989 after working as a caddie in his native Argentina.
Born in Cordoba, Argentina.
Won 2 major championships, two years apart.
Nicknamed 'El Pato' ('The Duck').
Beat Kenny Perry and Chad Campbell in a playoff to win the 2009 Masters.
Became the first golfer from Argentina ever to win a major, doing so at both the 2007 U.S. Open and 2009 Masters.

name: Y.E. Yang
hints: Turned pro in 1996 after starting golf relatively late as a teenager.
Born in Jeju, South Korea.
Won 1 major championship, the 2009 PGA Championship.
Hit a memorable hybrid approach shot on the final hole to seal his win.
Became the first golfer born in Asia ever to win a men's major title.
Achieved that win by defeating Tiger Woods in the final round, the only time in Tiger's career he lost a major after leading by himself through 54 holes.

name: Charl Schwartzel
hints: Turned pro in 2002 after a standout junior career in South Africa.
Born in Johannesburg, South Africa.
Won 1 major championship, the 2011 Masters.
Part of a strong generation of South African major champions.
Later became a prominent figure and event winner on LIV Golf.
Closed that Masters with four consecutive birdies on the back nine to snatch the win.

name: Bubba Watson
hints: Turned pro in 2003 and is entirely self-taught, having never taken a formal golf lesson.
Born in Bagdad, Florida.
Won 2 Masters titles, two years apart.
Also known for his pink driver and quirky, outspoken personality.
Plays left-handed despite doing most other things right-handed.
Famously won his first Masters in 2012 with a miracle hooking wedge shot from deep in the trees during a playoff.

name: Danny Willett
hints: Turned pro in 2008 after a strong amateur career in England.
Born in Sheffield, England.
Won 1 major championship, the 2016 Masters.
Nearly missed the tournament entirely, only playing because of the birth of his first son.
Became the first English golfer to win the Masters since Nick Faldo.
Capitalized on one of the most historic final-round collapses in major championship history to win that green jacket.

name: Patrick Reed
hints: Turned pro in 2011 after a standout, if controversial, college career.
Born in San Antonio, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 2018 Masters.
Later became one of the first prominent players to join LIV Golf.
Nicknamed 'Captain America' for his fiery Ryder Cup performances.
Held off a hard-charging Rickie Fowler down the stretch to win that Masters green jacket.

name: Gary Woodland
hints: Turned pro in 2007 after playing college basketball before switching fully to golf.
Born in Topeka, Kansas.
Won 1 major championship, the 2019 U.S. Open.
Known for elite athleticism and long drives off the tee.
Held off a hard-charging Brooks Koepka down the stretch to win at Pebble Beach.
Later underwent brain surgery in 2023 for a serious condition, then returned to competitive golf as an emotional comeback story.

name: Jason Day
hints: Turned pro in 2006 after emigrating from Australia to the U.S. as a teenager to train.
Born in Beaudesert, Australia.
Won 1 major championship, the 2015 PGA Championship.
Known for a distinctive pre-shot routine involving closed eyes and visualization.
Reached world No. 1 shortly after that breakthrough win.
Won that PGA Championship with a record-low score relative to par at the time.

name: Louis Oosthuizen
hints: Turned pro in 2002 and grew up near the same course as fellow South African stars.
Born in Mossel Bay, South Africa.
Won 1 major championship, the 2010 Open Championship.
Has finished runner-up at all four majors at various points in his career.
Later became a prominent LIV Golf player and team captain.
Won that Open at St Andrews by 7 shots, then years later made an ace on the par-5 second at Augusta after a shot deflected off the flagstick's base.

name: Wyndham Clark
hints: Turned pro in 2017 after college golf at Oregon and Oklahoma State.
Born in Denver, Colorado.
Won 1 major championship, the 2023 U.S. Open.
Broke through relatively late for a major winner, in his late 20s.
Has spoken openly about the loss of his mother as a driving motivation.
Held off Rory McIlroy down the stretch at Los Angeles Country Club to win that U.S. Open.

name: Brian Harman
hints: Turned pro in 2009 after a standout college career at Georgia.
Born in Savannah, Georgia.
Won 1 major championship, the 2023 Open Championship.
Plays left-handed and is known for elite bunker and scrambling skills.
Won wire-to-wire, leading after every single round of the tournament.
Won that Open at Royal Liverpool by six shots, a surprisingly dominant margin for a golfer not among the sport's biggest hitters.

name: Jason Dufner
hints: Turned pro in 2000 after college golf at Auburn.
Born in Cleveland, Ohio.
Won 1 major championship, the 2013 PGA Championship.
Known for a smooth, compact swing built for consistency.
Considered one of the more understated, low-key major champions of his era.
His slumped, disinterested-looking sitting pose once went viral online as a meme called 'Dufnering.'

name: Michael Campbell
hints: Turned pro in 1993 and represented New Zealand throughout his career.
Born in Hastings, New Zealand, of Maori descent.
Won 1 major championship, the 2005 U.S. Open.
His win remains one of the more surprising major upsets of the 2000s.
Became just the second golfer from New Zealand ever to win a men's major.
Beat Tiger Woods by two shots at Pinehurst to win that U.S. Open.

name: Ben Curtis
hints: Turned pro in 2000 and was playing in his very first major championship start.
Born in Ostrander, Ohio.
Won 1 major championship, the 2003 Open Championship.
His win stunned a leaderboard full of far more established stars.
Was ranked 396th in the world at the time, one of the biggest upsets in major history.
Remains the only golfer in history to win a major championship in his very first career start.

name: Trevor Immelman
hints: Turned pro in 1999 after a strong junior and amateur career in South Africa.
Born in Cape Town, South Africa.
Won 1 major championship, the 2008 Masters.
Later transitioned into a prominent role as a golf broadcaster.
Now a lead commentator for CBS's golf coverage.
Held off a hard-charging Tiger Woods in the final round to win that Masters green jacket.

name: Stewart Cink
hints: Turned pro in 1995 after college golf at Georgia Tech.
Born in Huntsville, Alabama.
Won 1 major championship, the 2009 Open Championship.
Known for his tall frame and easygoing demeanor.
Later became a two-time PGA Tour winner well into his 40s during the pandemic era.
Beat a 59-year-old Tom Watson in a playoff at Turnberry, denying Watson what would have been a storybook 6th Open title.

name: Graeme McDowell
hints: Turned pro in 2002 after a standout amateur career in Northern Ireland.
Born in Portrush, Northern Ireland.
Won 1 major championship, the 2010 U.S. Open.
Nicknamed 'G-Mac' by fans and broadcasters.
A key clutch performer for Europe across several Ryder Cups.
Became the first European golfer to win the U.S. Open in 40 years, doing so at Pebble Beach.

name: Darren Clarke
hints: Turned pro in 1990 and became one of Northern Ireland's most beloved golfers.
Born in Dungannon, Northern Ireland.
Won 1 major championship, the 2011 Open Championship.
A close friend and mentor figure to fellow Northern Irish stars Rory McIlroy and Graeme McDowell.
Later captained Europe's Ryder Cup team in 2016.
Won that Open at Royal St George's at age 42, a career-crowning achievement after years of near-misses.

name: Cameron Smith
hints: Turned pro in 2013 after a standout junior career in Australia.
Born in Brisbane, Australia.
Won 1 major championship, the 2022 Open Championship.
Instantly recognizable for his signature mullet hairstyle.
Left the PGA Tour to join LIV Golf shortly after that major win.
Shot a final-round 64 at the Old Course to overtake Cameron Young and Rory McIlroy and win that Open.

name: Jimmy Demaret
hints: Turned pro in the late 1920s and became known as one of golf's earliest style icons.
Born in Houston, Texas.
Won 3 Masters titles, across an 11-year span.
Famous for flamboyant, brightly colored outfits decades before it was common on tour.
Later co-hosted the pioneering TV series 'Shell's Wonderful World of Golf.'
Became the first three-time Masters champion in tournament history, winning in 1940, 1947, and 1950.

name: Cary Middlecoff
hints: Turned pro in 1947 after first earning a dentistry degree.
Born in Halls, Tennessee.
Won 3 major championships in the 1940s and 1950s.
Known for a deliberate, slow pre-shot routine that frustrated playing partners.
Nicknamed 'Doc' for his background as a practicing dentist.
Won 2 U.S. Opens, in 1949 and 1956, plus the 1955 Masters.

name: Billy Casper
hints: Turned pro in 1954 and quietly amassed 51 career PGA Tour wins.
Born in San Diego, California.
Won 3 major championships across the 1950s, 60s, and 70s.
Famous for an unusually delicate, soft putting touch.
Later followed an unconventional diet, including buffalo meat, for health reasons.
Won 2 U.S. Opens (1959, 1966) and the 1970 Masters, yet is often overlooked historically despite ranking among the winningest golfers ever.

name: Julius Boros
hints: Worked as an accountant before turning pro relatively late in his 20s.
Born in Fairfield, Connecticut, to Hungarian immigrant parents.
Won 3 major championships across a nearly 20-year span.
Known for an unhurried, relaxed swing that belied his competitiveness.
Won 2 U.S. Opens, in 1952 and 1963.
Became the oldest major champion in history at the time, winning the 1968 PGA Championship at age 48.

name: Ken Venturi
hints: Turned pro in 1957 after several near-misses as one of the top amateurs in the country.
Born in San Francisco, California.
Won 1 major championship, the 1964 U.S. Open.
Later became a longtime, respected lead golf analyst for CBS.
Doctors reportedly monitored him between rounds as he pushed through severe heat exhaustion.
Nearly collapsed from heat exhaustion while playing 36 holes in brutal heat on the final day at Congressional, yet still won.

name: Tony Jacklin
hints: Turned pro in 1962 and became Britain's first true global golf star in decades.
Born in Scunthorpe, England.
Won 2 major championships back-to-back.
Later captained Europe's Ryder Cup teams through their 1980s resurgence.
Was the first Englishman to win the U.S. Open in 50 years.
Held the Open Championship and U.S. Open titles simultaneously, having won the 1969 Open and 1970 U.S. Open in consecutive majors.

name: Johnny Miller
hints: Turned pro in 1969 after a standout amateur career in San Francisco.
Born in San Francisco, California.
Won 2 major championships, three years apart.
Later became one of golf broadcasting's most blunt, opinionated lead analysts.
Known during his playing peak for extraordinarily precise iron play.
Shot a final-round 63 at Oakmont to win the 1973 U.S. Open, still regarded as one of the greatest closing rounds in major championship history.

name: Andy North
hints: Turned pro in 1972 after college golf at the University of Florida.
Born in Thorp, Wisconsin.
Won 2 U.S. Open championships, seven years apart.
Later became a respected golf broadcaster.
Considered one of the more surprising multi-major champions relative to overall career record.
Won both his U.S. Opens, in 1978 and 1985, despite totaling only 3 PGA Tour wins in his entire career.

name: Fuzzy Zoeller
hints: Turned pro in 1973 and became known for an easygoing, whistling demeanor on course.
Born in New Albany, Indiana.
Won 2 major championships, five years apart.
Nicknamed 'Fuzzy,' a childhood nickname derived from his middle name Urban.
Also won the 1984 U.S. Open in an 18-hole playoff.
Won the 1979 Masters in a playoff in just his first career appearance at Augusta, one of very few golfers ever to do so.

name: Craig Stadler
hints: Turned pro in 1975 after winning the U.S. Amateur.
Born in San Diego, California.
Won 1 major championship, the 1982 Masters.
Later found continued success on the PGA Tour Champions.
Nicknamed 'The Walrus' for his mustache and burly build.
Years after his Masters win, was penalized on tour for kneeling on a towel to keep his pants clean, ruled as illegally building a stance.

name: Larry Mize
hints: Turned pro in 1980 and grew up just down the road from the course that made him famous.
Born and raised in Augusta, Georgia.
Won 1 major championship, the 1987 Masters.
Remains one of the most replayed moments in Masters broadcast history.
Won with a stunning long chip-in on the second hole of a playoff.
That chip-in beat a devastated Greg Norman, considered one of the cruelest playoff losses in major championship history.

name: Scott Simpson
hints: Turned pro in 1977 after winning the NCAA individual title at USC.
Born in San Diego, California.
Won 1 major championship, the 1987 U.S. Open.
Known for a steady, error-free style of play.
One of several U.S. Open champions produced from San Diego's golf scene.
Held off a hard-charging Tom Watson down the stretch at the Olympic Club to win that U.S. Open.

name: Tom Kite
hints: Turned pro in 1972 after a celebrated rivalry with Ben Crenshaw at the University of Texas.
Born in Austin, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 1992 U.S. Open.
Known for meticulous course preparation and a gritty, grinding style.
Spent years as one of the tour's most consistent money leaders before that breakthrough.
Later captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in 1997, having won his lone major in brutal wind at Pebble Beach.

name: Lee Janzen
hints: Turned pro in 1986 after college golf at Florida Southern.
Born in Austin, Minnesota, and raised in Florida.
Won 2 U.S. Open championships, five years apart.
Known for clutch final-round performances in majors.
Both of his major wins came at the expense of the same golfer.
Beat Payne Stewart to win the U.S. Open twice, in 1993 and again in 1998 after trailing him by 5 shots entering the final round.

name: Steve Jones
hints: Turned pro in 1981 and missed nearly two full years after a serious dirt-bike injury to his hand.
Born in Phoenix, Arizona.
Won 1 major championship, the 1996 U.S. Open.
Had to requalify for tour events after his time away from the game.
A determined grinder who rebuilt his career from the ground up after his injury.
Completed one of the most remarkable injury-comeback stories in golf history by winning that U.S. Open at Oakland Hills.

name: Justin Rose
hints: Turned pro at just 17 years old in 1998, right after a famous amateur performance at the Open.
Born in Johannesburg, South Africa, and raised in England.
Won 1 major championship, the 2013 U.S. Open.
Spent years as one of the most consistent top-10 major finishers without winning more.
Known for a smooth, classically sound swing.
Also won the individual Olympic gold medal in golf's return to the Games in 2016, having won his lone major at Merion in 2013.

name: Martin Kaymer
hints: Turned pro in 2006 and quickly rose to world No. 1 by his mid-20s.
Born in Dusseldorf, Germany.
Won 2 major championships, four years apart.
One of Germany's most successful golfers alongside Bernhard Langer.
Also holed the Ryder Cup-clinching putt for Europe at the 2012 'Miracle at Medinah.'
Won the 2010 PGA Championship in a playoff, then led the 2014 U.S. Open at Pinehurst from start to finish in dominant fashion.

name: Bobby Locke
hints: Turned pro in the late 1930s and became South Africa's first true golfing superstar.
Born in Germiston, South Africa.
Won 4 Open Championships between 1949 and 1957.
Helped establish South Africa as a major golfing nation decades before Player and Els.
Played with a distinctive hooded putting style that produced remarkable consistency.
Widely regarded as one of the greatest putters the game has ever seen, using a closed, hooded stroke that mystified rivals for two decades.

name: Peter Thomson
hints: Turned pro in 1946 and dominated links golf through the 1950s and 1960s.
Born in Melbourne, Australia.
Won 5 Open Championships between 1954 and 1965.
Rarely played full-time in the United States, focusing instead on Britain and Australasia.
Later became a respected golf course architect and writer.
Won 3 Open Championships in a row, from 1954 through 1956, a feat matched by very few golfers in the tournament's long history.

name: Kel Nagle
hints: Turned pro in the mid-1940s after growing up in Sydney, Australia.
Born in Sydney, Australia.
Won 1 major championship, the 1960 Centenary Open Championship.
Enjoyed one of the longest competitive careers in golf history, playing into his 70s.
A close friend and rival of fellow Australian Peter Thomson.
Edged Arnold Palmer by a single shot at St Andrews to win that historic 100th-anniversary Open.

name: Roberto De Vicenzo
hints: Turned pro in the late 1930s and became one of Argentina's most beloved sporting figures.
Born in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
Won 1 major championship, the 1967 Open Championship.
Remains one of the most universally admired figures in golf history.
The following year, signed an incorrect scorecard at the Masters that cost him a place in a playoff.
Edged Jack Nicklaus to win that Open at Hoylake, then handled his Masters scorecard heartbreak with such grace it became a legendary story of sportsmanship.

name: Tom Weiskopf
hints: Turned pro in 1968 after college golf at Ohio State, the same program as Jack Nicklaus.
Born in Massillon, Ohio.
Won 1 major championship, the 1973 Open Championship.
Later became a respected golf course architect and TV commentator.
Known for a fiery temperament paired with one of the purest swings of his generation.
Finished runner-up at the Masters an agonizing four times in his career, despite winning that 1973 Open at Royal Troon.

name: Bill Rogers
hints: Turned pro in 1974 after college golf at the University of Houston.
Born in Waco, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 1981 Open Championship.
His rapid rise and quick decline remains a cautionary tale often cited in golf.
Burned out from the pressure of stardom and faded from top competitive golf soon after.
Capped a remarkable career year, that included a World Match Play title, by winning that Open at Royal St George's.

name: Mark Calcavecchia
hints: Turned pro in 1981 after college golf at the University of Florida.
Born in Laurel, Nebraska.
Won 1 major championship, the 1989 Open Championship.
Remained a fixture on the PGA Tour and later PGA Tour Champions for decades.
Known for a long, looping swing and a fiery personality.
Beat Greg Norman and Wayne Grady in a four-hole aggregate playoff at Royal Troon to win that Open.

name: Ian Baker-Finch
hints: Turned pro in 1979 after a strong junior career in Australia.
Born in Nambour, Australia.
Won 1 major championship, the 1991 Open Championship.
Successfully transitioned afterward into a respected TV broadcasting career.
Later suffered one of the most public and severe driving slumps in professional golf.
That collapse eventually forced him out of competitive golf entirely, despite once being Open champion at Royal Birkdale.

name: Nick Price
hints: Turned pro in 1977 and represented Zimbabwe throughout his career.
Born in Durban, South Africa, raised in Zimbabwe.
Won 3 major championships in a remarkably short span in the early-to-mid 1990s.
Widely regarded as one of the fastest, most efficient players of any era.
Reached world No. 1 during his dominant mid-1990s stretch.
Won the 1992 and 1994 PGA Championships plus the 1994 Open Championship, three majors within a three-year window.

name: John Daly
hints: Turned pro in 1987 and became famous almost overnight for enormous driving distance.
Born in Carmichael, California.
Won 2 major championships, four years apart.
Later became known for loud pants and a clothing line as much as his golf.
Known for the motto 'grip it and rip it' and a colorful, unpredictable off-course life.
Won the 1991 PGA Championship as the ninth alternate with almost no practice rounds, then won the 1995 Open Championship at St Andrews in a playoff.

name: David Duval
hints: Turned pro in 1993 after a decorated college career at Georgia Tech.
Born in Jacksonville, Florida.
Won 1 major championship, the 2001 Open Championship.
Experienced one of the most dramatic competitive declines of any recent world No. 1.
Known for wraparound sunglasses and a stoic, unreadable on-course demeanor.
Shot a final-round 59 in a PGA Tour event during his dominant 1999 peak, reaching world No. 1 before winning that Open at Royal Lytham.

name: Todd Hamilton
hints: Turned pro in the late 1980s and spent many years playing in Asia before reaching the PGA Tour.
Born in Galesburg, Illinois.
Won 1 major championship, the 2004 Open Championship.
Remains one of the more unexpected major champions of the 2000s.
Famously used a hybrid-style club around the greens instead of a traditional chipping technique.
Beat Ernie Els in a four-hole playoff at Royal Troon to win that Open.

name: Lanny Wadkins
hints: Turned pro in 1971 after winning the U.S. Amateur.
Born in Richmond, Virginia.
Won 1 major championship, the 1977 PGA Championship.
Became one of the most passionate and successful Ryder Cup competitors of his generation.
Later captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in 1995.
Known for an aggressive, fast-paced style of play, won that PGA Championship in a playoff over Gene Littler.

name: Larry Nelson
hints: Didn't pick up golf seriously until after serving in the Vietnam War in his early 20s.
Born in Fort Payne, Alabama.
Won 3 major championships despite starting the game unusually late.
One of the more remarkable late-starting success stories in professional golf.
Later found continued success on the PGA Tour Champions.
Won the 1981 and 1987 PGA Championships plus the 1983 U.S. Open.

name: Hal Sutton
hints: Turned pro in 1981 after winning both the U.S. Amateur and NCAA title.
Born in Shreveport, Louisiana.
Won 1 major championship, the 1983 PGA Championship.
Captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in 2004.
Known for a confident, sometimes brash competitive style.
Was touted as the game's next big star after that PGA win, and later had a famous head-to-head duel with Tiger Woods down the stretch at a non-major event in 2000.

name: Steve Elkington
hints: Turned pro in 1985 after college golf at the University of Houston.
Born in Wagga Wagga, Australia.
Won 1 major championship, the 1995 PGA Championship.
Battled sinus issues throughout his career that occasionally affected his play.
A frequent teaching reference for swing coaches even after retirement.
Widely regarded as having one of the most technically pure, textbook swings in golf history, won that PGA in a playoff over Colin Montgomerie.

name: Mark Brooks
hints: Turned pro in 1984 after college golf at the University of Texas.
Born in Fort Worth, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 1996 PGA Championship.
Remained a steady tour presence for years without matching that major success again.
Known for a workmanlike, unflashy approach to the game.
Won that PGA Championship in a playoff over Kenny Perry, one of several Texas products to win a major in the 1990s.

name: David Toms
hints: Turned pro in 1989 after college golf at LSU.
Born in Monroe, Louisiana.
Won 1 major championship, the 2001 PGA Championship.
Known for excellent course management and a smooth, compact swing.
Famously laid up short of the water on the final hole rather than risk going for the green.
Got up and down from there to win that PGA Championship at Atlanta Athletic Club by one shot over Phil Mickelson.

name: Rich Beem
hints: Once sold car stereos before turning his focus fully to professional golf.
Born in Phoenix, Arizona.
Won 1 major championship, the 2002 PGA Championship.
Remains one of the more unlikely major champions of the 2000s.
Known for a fun-loving, unpolished personality relative to typical tour pros.
Held off a furious final-round charge from Tiger Woods at Hazeltine to win that PGA Championship.

name: Shaun Micheel
hints: Turned pro in 1992 and spent years grinding on developmental tours before his breakthrough.
Born in Orlando, Florida.
Won 1 major championship, the 2003 PGA Championship.
Recorded only one other PGA Tour win across the rest of his career.
Sealed the win with a stunning approach shot on the final hole.
That approach at Oak Hill finished two inches from the cup, remaining one of the most memorable clutch shots in major championship history.

name: Jimmy Walker
hints: Turned pro in 2001 after college golf at Baylor.
Born in Abilene, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 2016 PGA Championship.
Broke through relatively late in his career, in his late 30s.
Known for a smooth tempo and reliable ball-striking during his peak years.
Was later diagnosed with a chronic autoimmune condition that affected his playing career, having won his lone major at Baltusrol.

name: Mike Weir
hints: Turned pro in 1992 after a standout amateur and college career.
Born in Sarnia, Ontario, Canada.
Won 1 major championship, the 2003 Masters.
One of the most prominent left-handed golfers to reach the top of the sport.
His Masters win remains a landmark moment for Canadian golf.
Became the first Canadian man ever to win a men's major, doing so in a playoff over Len Mattiace.
